newsitem.title: USA: IBM CEO says utilities need to know market.
newsitem.headline: IBM CEO says utilities need to know market.

text.p: IBM chief executive officer Louis V. Gerstner Jr called for U.S. electric utilities to make better use of market data to serve their customers as the industry continues to deregulate.
"Your business model is changing...(Information) technology will be the manifestation of your brand," said Gerstner here Monday at the annual Edison Electric Institute Convention/Expo.
It is paramount for utilities to understand and anticipate customer needs to compete effectively in a deregulated environment, Gerstner said.
"It will determine winners and losers of the next century," he said.

Gerstner said "data-mining", or digging through mountains of seeming unrelated information on customers, is necessary work as utilities face new competition from new players such as marketers and brokers and regulators are giving consumers choice to select their power suppliers.
By using current information technology, utilities could retrieve data and analyze issues that they did not face under regulation such as consumer behavior, Gerstner said.
In the days before deregulation, utilities merely had to worry over total usage, demand increase and "keeping the lights on," Gerstner said.
Electric companies could use the data to tailor their products and services to specific customer groups as well as drive down their costs of operations, he said.
Manual intensive tasks like meter-reading can be automated, he added.
